{"notes": "Visit 3 (7:15): The picture shows the whole fish dark. Both body arcs, the tail junction (~x23) and both fins are connected, with no pale or detached pieces. Leo's claim that the run connects nose to both tail fins matches what I see. Still, I never saw who placed what, so individual credit rests on self-reports and how well accounts agree. The tail joint is dense and clustered, so it could be fragile at the push. Only Leo spoke this visit; the others stayed quiet and hands-off.

Priya: Led the plan. She says she sketched the fish, split the strokes, laid the top line, and inspected and fixed the tail joint. Her top line was accurate and on pace. She set the hands-off rule and a bump plan. Others credit her consistently. Caveats: her checks were visual, and her 'extra dominoes are the only way to break it' claim was overconfident. Leadership and ownership are high.

Tom: Says he laid the top tail stroke and checked the run, and Priya's account matches except for a small mismatch over who did which tail fin. His work is unwitnessed and his '98 of 98' count is unverified. He was silent with me earlier and silent again this visit. Moderate rating, pending the push.

Leo: Strong overview, and he gave the clearest status update this visit. He likely did the lower tail, since Priya and Tom both say so. He traced the run by eye, kept hands off, and offered to restand anything knocked. Good coordination and collaboration.

Maya: The bottom line is confirmed by the picture and by others' accounts. Clean, reliable work and an appropriate hands-off stance. Somewhat passive, with less initiative and leadership. Silent this visit.

Shared gap: everyone verified by eye only, and nobody tested the joint. The push is the real test."}
